frontmatter.title: Introduction to SIMD instructions on x86-64

children.value: Modern x86-64 CPUs can operate not only on
values (one integer or floating-point number at a time), but also on
(Single Instruction, Multiple Data) instructions. SIMD instructions allow the same arithmetic operation to be applied simultaneously to multiple data elements packed inside a single register.

This capability is central to high-performance numerical code and is one of the main reasons why optimized code can outperform naïve implementations by an order of magnitude or more, even when the algorithm itself is unchanged.

SIMD, loop unrolling, and associative algebra
In scalar execution, a CPU instruction operates on a single data element:
Here, one floating-point addition is performed per instruction.
In SIMD execution, a single instruction operates on multiple data elements packed in a wider register:

scalar:  s += a[i]

SIMD:    s[0..3] += a[i..i+3]
The instruction count may be similar, but the
amount of work done per instruction
is higher. This is the fundamental source of SIMD speedups.
